title: Pad Krapow
subtitle: Thai holy basil stir-fry with pork and a fried egg
excerpt: Thailand's beloved street food: pork mince stir-fried at high heat with garlic, fresh chillies, oyster sauce, and fish sauce, finished with a large amount of holy basil, served over jasmine rice with a crispy fried egg. Fast, fragrant, and intensely savoury.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pad krapow (stir-fried holy basil) is arguably the most frequently eaten dish in Thailand, the default lunch order for office workers across Bangkok and the most common street food at the stalls that set up on every corner at midday. Krapow refers to holy basil (Ocimum tenuiflorum), a different variety from sweet Italian basil with a distinctly different, more peppery, clove-like flavour. If holy basil is unavailable, Thai basil is the best substitute; Italian basil is a distant last resort. The dish is made with any protein, but pork mince (mu) and chicken mince (gai) are the most common. The fried egg (kai dao, star egg) is the canonical accompaniment, fried in a centimetre of very hot oil so the white blisters and crisps at the edges while the yolk stays runny. The dish takes about 5 minutes to cook and must be eaten immediately.

recipeTools.notes: A wok is essential for the high-heat stir-fry; a regular frying pan produces a less intense result.

content.text: Cook over the highest possible heat throughout. The wok should be smoking hot before any ingredient goes in. Add the basil at the very end, off the heat if needed; it wilts in seconds and should retain some texture. The dish is served immediately; it does not wait.

items.preparation: leaves picked; or holy basil if available
fresh; birds eye chillies preferred; roughly chopped

content.text: Mix the oyster sauce, fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar in a small bowl. Set aside. Heat a wok over the highest heat until very hot and beginning to smoke. Add 2 tablespoons of oil. Add the garlic and chilli and stir-fry for 30 seconds; it will sizzle and colour quickly.

Add the pork mince and stir-fry, breaking it apart, for 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through and lightly caramelised in places. Pour in the sauce mixture and toss to coat. Cook for 30 seconds more. Remove from the heat. Add the basil leaves and toss quickly; they will wilt in the residual heat.

In a separate small pan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil over high heat until very hot. Crack in the eggs and fry until the whites are fully set and crisped at the edges but the yolks are still runny, about 2 minutes. Serve the pork over rice with a fried egg on top.
